bug_info.bug_desc: In FastPwrStateAckPwrUp, the wake interrupt output wkup_o was asserted whenever the slow FSM power-up cause was Wake, without also checking the fast FSM's recorded reset cause. Per the specification, a wake interrupt should only be generated when exiting low power due to a wake event and the previous reset cause was LowPwrEntry. If the power-up is caused by a reset event, no wake interrupt should be generated. The old expression could therefore assert a spurious wakeup interrupt after a reset-recovery or hardware-reset power-up if the slow FSM's most recent low-power exit had been reported as a wake event. The root cause is a missing qualifier in the boolean expression for wkup_o.
bug_info.fix_hint: Qualify the wake interrupt generation with both the slow FSM power-up cause and the fast FSM reset cause. Specifically, assert wkup_o only when pwrup_cause_i is Wake and reset_cause_q is LowPwrEntry. This ensures regular reset-recovery power-ups do not generate a wakeup interrupt.
